chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Shu'ayb al-Haddad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Dissimulation (Taqiyya) was instituted only to preserve blood (from being spilled). So when the blood is to be spilled anyway, then it is no longer dissimulation.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: Dissimulation or concealment of faith to avoid harm
key_terms.الدَّمُ: Blood, referring to life or the act of killing
key_terms.بَلَغَ: Reached or arrived at (in the sense of certainty)
key_terms.لِيُحْقَنَ: To be preserved or saved (specifically blood/life)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition under which Taqiyya is no longer applicable according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that Taqiyya is a pragmatic shield for preserving life, but it is not an absolute mandate; once death becomes inevitable, the protective veil is lifted, and one should not conceal faith to delay the inevitable. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the permissibility of concealment and the obligation of martyrdom, emphasizing that the preservation of life is the primary objective but not at the cost of denying truth when death is certain. The ruling reflects the dynamic nature of Taqiyya, which is context-dependent rather than a static state of being.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Shuayb Al Haddad, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘But rather, the dissimulation (Taqiyya) has been Made to be for saving the blood by it. So when it comes to the blood (to be spilt anyway), then there would be no dissimulation (Taqiyya)’.
en.sarwar: 16. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Shu’ayb al-Haddad from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:
“ Al-Taqiyyah is made law to save lives. Once it (danger) is already there to take lives, then there is no al-Taqiyyah .”
